suburbs.name: Katy
suburbs.housingCharacter: Large HOA-governed master-planned communities: Cinco Ranch opened in 1991 with most homes having four to five bedrooms and brick construction the norm; Elyson is a 3,600-acre development of roughly 1,500 new-construction homes with typical floorplans around 2,800 sq ft, and Firethorne has been building since 2005 on 1,400 acres with construction still ongoing.

conditions.condition: Homes of 2,800 sq ft and up with four to five bedrooms in gate-and-amenity communities
conditions.implication: Multi-bathroom, multi-storey jobs that require longer crew hours

conditions.condition: Backyard pools and lake/greenbelt frontage
conditions.implication: Tracked-in grass and pool water at back doors

conditions.condition: Newer housing stock with lots of glass and hard-surface floor
conditions.implication: Fewer deferred-maintenance surprises but more glass and hard floor to clean

suburbs.name: Sugar Land
suburbs.housingCharacter: First Colony is an umbrella master plan spanning 9,700 acres with over 60,000 residents and nearly 14,000 homes, 1,700 apartments, 750 townhomes and 169 condos across 61-plus subdivisions; Sweetwater is an upscale golf-course neighborhood of roughly 570 households built around Sweetwater Country Club, and Telfair is one of Sugar Land's newest neighborhoods with 250-plus acres of parks and lakes.

conditions.condition: A single HOA umbrella covering tens of thousands of similar households
conditions.implication: Strong referral network — one satisfied street in First Colony reaches many comparable homes

conditions.condition: Housing ranges from condo and townhome to golf-course estate
conditions.implication: Quote ranges have to be wide to cover the spread of home types

conditions.condition: Golf-course frontage
conditions.implication: Turf chemicals and clippings tracked in at entryways

suburbs.name: Pearland
suburbs.housingCharacter: Most residential areas sit inside planned communities governed by HOAs that maintain neighborhood standards; Shadow Creek Ranch covers 3,500 acres on a lake theme and was built out by production builders including Perry, Meritage, Coventry, Westin, Ashton Woods and D.R. Horton.

conditions.condition: Production-builder stock with repeating floorplans
conditions.implication: A crew that learns one Shadow Creek plan can price the next one accurately

conditions.condition: Lake-and-canal layout across 3,500 acres
conditions.implication: Standing water and added humidity right at the property line

conditions.condition: Roughly 10 miles from the Texas Medical Center, with shift-working medical households
conditions.implication: Favours keyed or coded access and flexible scheduling

suburbs.name: The Woodlands
suburbs.housingCharacter: Nine residential villages of very different ages — Grogan's Mill was founded in 1974 and now holds over 12,000 residents, while College Park and Creekside Park are among the newer sections. The area is known for heavy tree cover, parks and nature trails.

conditions.condition: Wide age spread between villages
conditions.implication: A 1970s Grogan's Mill house and a Creekside Park house are different cleaning jobs

conditions.condition: Dense tree canopy and shade
conditions.implication: Exteriors, patios and north-facing rooms stay damp

conditions.condition: Extensive trail network and leaf litter
conditions.implication: Leaf litter and pollen come in on shoes

conditions.condition: Residents identify by village, not by "The Woodlands"
conditions.implication: Sell and market the villages by name

suburbs.name: Missouri City
suburbs.housingCharacter: Southwest of Houston and adjacent to Sugar Land, with the First Colony community overlapping into the city; no further housing-stock detail was verified.

suburbs.name: Memorial
suburbs.housingCharacter: The Memorial Corridor on the west side has been redeveloping toward more residential use, with CityCentre — a mixed-use development — producing a range of new residential options; the established housing itself was not described.

conditions.condition: A newer condo and townhome component alongside established housing
conditions.implication: Mixed job types between compact new units and older established homes

conditions.condition: Subtropical climate, with most of Greater Houston in USDA plant hardiness zone 9 — long, hot, muggy summers and mild winter lows barely below freezing, with no hard freeze season and no dry season
conditions.implication: No seasonal break in soil load; cleaning demand and moisture conditions run all twelve months

conditions.condition: High humidity makes Houston a hotspot for dust mite and mold allergens, which are perennial and year-round; high humidity, frequent rainfall and warm temperatures let mold thrive in hidden places, and indoor humidity is best held at 30–50%
conditions.implication: Bathrooms never fully dry out, so grout, caulk lines, shower glass and window tracks discolour faster than owners expect and need scrubbing on a shorter cycle than in a dry climate; closets, under-sink cabinets and any room behind a closed door hold moisture; dust-mite load in mattresses, upholstery and drapes is a year-round problem

conditions.condition: Air conditioning runs nearly all year and the units themselves can harbor mold without regular maintenance
conditions.implication: Supply and return vents, registers and the surrounding ceiling get visibly dirty and are worth listing as an add-on service

conditions.condition: Mold spore counts across southeast Texas hit the extreme category at the end of January, driven by damp, foggy mornings — mold peaks in winter here, not summer
conditions.implication: Winter is not a slow, clean season in Houston; late January is a mold peak and should be worked accordingly

conditions.condition: Pollen season runs nearly the whole year: tree pollen starts as early as December, mountain cedar drives cedar fever in January, oak, pine, ash, elm, pecan and mulberry peak February through April with oak visibly blanketing the city in yellow, and grass pollen — Bermuda, Johnson, Bahia, ryegrass — takes over from late April through summer into early fall, with Bermuda producing symptoms into October
conditions.implication: February–April is the visible-yellow-film season on sills, entry floors, ceiling fans and anything near a door; sell recurring service on the basis that there is no month without an airborne load

conditions.condition: Alternaria and Cladosporium moulds run year-round alongside dust mites and urban ozone
conditions.implication: Allergy-driven demand is real and is not confined to spring, supporting year-round recurring plans
